newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gabon desperately seeking new oil reserves.
newsitem.headline: Gabon desperately seeking new oil reserves.

text.p: Gabon needed to discover new oil reserves to counter declining production, Samual Dossou-Aworet, chairman of Petrolin UK and government adviser for petroleum affairs said on Wednesday.
He forecast that Gabon's total offshore and onshore oil production would decline to 155,000 barrels per day (bpd0 by the year 2004 from a current 355,000 bpd.

"To find new reserves in order to counterbalance the natural decline in production is a major problem for Gabon, at a time where exploration has quite exhausted the classical themes of research," Dossou-Aworet said.
Speaking at the Africa Upstream 1996 conference, he said numerous new possibilities were being implemented which could facilitate the development of new reserves.
Depleted and marginal fields were being either reactivated or sold by operators and the government was selling its stake in local oil companies, he said.

"The policy of the Gabonese government is therefore to look for new investors, to incite them to come and invest in the oil industry, and to encourage all projects which could lead to slow the decline of the production," he said.
Dossou-Aworet also urged Gabon to encourage gas exploration.
